chapter: Other Philadelphia work and the union
title: Miller and Polk as the first true jazz bands he worked with
summary: Waters is unsure whether Polk or Miller came first, but both were jazz bands in contrast to his brother's society work and the Waltz Dream dance band.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: OK, let's jump back to Philadelphia and your early career. You keep referring to Charlie Miller's Jazz Orchestra - do you mean that it was a jazz orchestra or do you mean they used the name "jazz" in their billing?
Yeah, yeah. Charlie Johnson's Jazz Band, you know.

Yeah, yeah. Yeah, because we were playing jazz. You see, there's a big difference from the dance hall thing. And my brother, too - see, we were playing jazz. The only band that's a, that's the first jazz band that I ever worked with in my life. The other bands was, you would say commercial. My brother -
So you worked with Miller before you worked with Polk then.
No, I worked with, I think I worked with Polk before -
Well, you said Polk wasn't a jazz band -
Well, they both were jazz bands -
So then Polk was the first jazz band you worked with -
Yeah, it could have been. No, I could be, made a mistake on the time that I

worked with Polk. And I know that with Charlie Miller I worked three days a week, but with Polk it wasn't no job. So I could even have been working with Polk at the same time because we only worked three days a week, understand what I mean?
You see, that I don't know, I can't pinpoint that.

But those two bands, I worked and they both were jazz bands. And the others was commercial. My brother, first thing I worked with my brother before anybody playing alto saxophone and reading music and playing popular numbers and songs from the shows like Shubert's Theater, Shubert's, you know, things like popular numbers for rich people. And we had to play the melody and I was playing little countermelodies and with his trumpet and real soft, muted. That's what I was doing before all of this. Well, that was thing like before me, see (laughs). Then after I got established a little bit in Philadelphia, I worked in this Waltz Dream and I still wasn't happy because I'm playing the music, still playing the music. Even I wasn't happy - I was happy with my brother because I could, we only had a trumpet and one saxophone. But in the band we had two saxophone and a trumpet and had the music, we had these restrain, you know, to this music. I did it, I did it. But then I got up with this Polk and this Charlie Miller deal. Then I was happy, for that was, they were strictly jazz. Riffs and things, just like they do now, and particularly the mainstream bands like Buddy Tate, things like that - (sings), that's what we doing. And with Polk it was the same thing, we were doing jazz. And we didn't - first thing, we didn't have that much music, those two bands.
